title: The degree-zero localization of a polynomial ring at a variable is a polynomial ring
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $n\ge0$, $S=A[T_0,\dots,T_n]$ graded by total degree, $j\in\{0,\dots,n\}$, and $S_{(T_j)}$ the degree-zero part of $S_{T_j}=S[1/T_j]$ [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero], i.e. the ring of fractions $a/T_j^m$ with $a\in S$ homogeneous of degree $m$. Let $A[Y_l:l
eq j]$ be the polynomial ring over $A$ in $n$ variables. Then the $A$-algebra map $	heta_j:A[Y_l:l
eq j]	o S_{(T_j)}$, $Y_l\mapsto T_l/T_j$, is an isomorphism; its inverse sends $a/T_j^m$ ($a$ homogeneous of degree $m$) to the dehomogenization $a(Y_0,\dots,Y_{j-1},1,Y_{j+1},\dots,Y_n)$. In particular the $n$ elements $T_l/T_j$, $l
eq j$, are algebraically independent over $A$ and generate $S_{(T_j)}$ as an $A$-algebra.
